decisions.reason: Replacing controlled fillable text fields with ordinary editable text makes the prior content-control-style automatic placeholder clearing behavior obsolete.
Ordinary editable text can still use a grey visual cue, but it is unclear whether the accepted grey field appearance depended on content-control shading or should be replaced.
The Title field's formatting-retention requirement remains applicable when text is represented as ordinary editable text.
Persistent help labels can accompany ordinary editable text and are not changed by removing content controls from text-entry fields.
The source decision concerns ordinary text-entry representation, not the independently accepted checklist control.
The source decision concerns ordinary text-entry representation and does not disable or alter the separate board-meeting dropdown control.
Selecting ordinary editable text does not change the established legacy-content transfer workflow or its layout and style stability criteria.
The ability to create manual line breaks after pasted content remains required regardless of the text-entry field representation.
Theme color availability is independent of whether ordinary text-entry areas use content controls.
The architecture change does not alter the requirement for stable rendering across users or the supported Word environment.
Pasted-table containment and layout stability are independent of the representation selected for ordinary text-entry fields.
Bullet sizing, alignment, balance, reference design, and color are unaffected by the ordinary text-entry architecture decision.
